small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose kernel has a correctness bug: it computes `kd = (od + PAD) % STRIDE` but then derives `id_val = (od + PAD - kd) // STRIDE`, which only picks one of the up-to-KD valid kernel taps. With STRIDE=2, KD=3, PAD=1, two values of kd (e.g. 0 and 2) can both produce valid id_val for the same od — the kernel must loop over all KD/KH/KW taps that satisfy `(od+PAD-kd) % STRIDE == 0` and accumulate, not pick a single one.
- After fixing, replace the per-lane `kw_vec` weight gather with a static loop over `kd, kh, kw` (each compile-time small: 3) so weight loads become contiguous `[OC]` vectors per (kd,kh,kw,ic) and input loads become per-lane gathers along `iw` only.
- Keep `BLOCK_OW=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3` as a starting config and prune the BLOCK_OW=32 entries; OC=16 is small so the OC-dim of the accumulator is cheap.
large_guidance:
- Redesign the conv_transpose as a direct gather kernel that loops over all (kd, kh, kw) taps satisfying the stride-divisibility condition, accumulating contributions from each valid input position. With KD=KH=KW=3 and STRIDE=2, at most 2 taps per spatial axis are valid per output coordinate (≤8 input contributions), so a static unrolled triple-loop with masks is the right structure — not the single-tap formula currently used.
- Tile over (N, OC, OD*OH*OW) with one program per (n, ow-tile, oh) and have OC fully resident (OC=16 fits in one lane); precompute valid (kd, ih, kw, …) masks outside the IC loop, then iterate IC inside. Fuse Swish into the epilogue before store.
- Consider channels_last (NDHWC) layout for the conv output so that the subsequent GroupNorm reduces along contiguous channel-group memory; alternatively, fuse the conv-transpose-Swish output directly into the GroupNorm partial-sum kernel via a two-pass scheme to eliminate one full read of the 128×16×32×64×64 tensor.
